title: Praise Waits in Zion, Lord, for Thee
description: Praise Waits in Zion, Lord, for Thee in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Edward Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 45 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Devout Worship of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise waits in Zi-on, Lord, for thee; Thy saints a-dore thy ho-ly name; Thy crea-tures bend th'obe-di-ent knee, And, hum-bly, thy pro-tec-tion claim.

lines: Praise waits in Zion, Lord, for thee;
Thy saints adore thy holy name;
Thy creatures bend th' obedient knee,
Thy hand has raised us from the dust;
The breath of life thy Spirit gave;
Where, but in thee, can mortals trust?
Who, but our God, has power to save?
Still may thy children in thy word
Their common trust and refuge see;
O bind us to each other, Lord,
By one great tie, — the love of thee.
So shall our sun of hope arise,
With brighter still and brighter ray,
Till thou shalt bless our longing eyes

licence: Public domain: James Edward Smith died in 1828.
credits: Words by James Edward Smith (1759–1828), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
